triggers: Before a stable jQStar major release
When an OpenJS project status changes
When a reviewed project publishes a stable release or changes support policy
When the OpenJS trademark policy or written permission changes
reviewPolicy.changeProcess: Recheck primary sources, update this matrix and its downstream digest through a ticket, then rerun static, package, and delivery gates.

product.positioning: An independent HTML-first UI and application library for jQuery.
product.disclaimer: jQStar is not affiliated with, sponsored by, endorsed by, or an official successor to the jQuery project or the OpenJS Foundation.
product.attribution: jQuery and related project names are trademarks of the OpenJS Foundation or their respective owners and are used here only for factual compatibility and migration statements.
allowedUses: Factual compatibility statements backed by current tests
Migration guidance that identifies the source and destination products
Ownership attribution and links to official project sources

surfaceReview.result: The package uses the independent jquery-star name and factual powered-by-jQuery wording; it declares jQuery only as a peer.
The README describes real-jQuery compatibility and migration without an official-project, endorsement, or drop-in jQuery UI claim.
Titles lead with jQStar; ecosystem names appear only in status, compatibility, attribution, and migration copy.
The custom jQStar mark and social card contain no copied jQuery or OpenJS logo or trade dress.
The public repository and package keywords make no official, successor, stewardship, sponsorship, or endorsement claim.
Examples use jQStar markup and APIs; no archived project runtime, logo, theme, or Widget Factory implementation is copied.
Guides distinguish factual source-project status from jQStar policy and assign executable migration claims to downstream tickets.
Current release surfaces make no third-party ownership claim; ticket 0017 must recheck this matrix before stable-major wording.

futureProposalPrerequisites: A concrete governance, security, maintenance, and funding plan
Explicit written agreement from the jQuery project and OpenJS Foundation

projects.name: jQuery Core
projects.maintenanceStatement: jQuery 4.x is current and only the latest jQuery release is fully supported; 3.x receives critical security patches and bug fixes.
projects.jqstarRole: The application-owned real jQuery instance is jQStar's sole selector, event, collection, and plugin foundation.
nonGoals: Changing the invariant that $ is jQuery while $name is a signal
recheckTriggers: A jQuery stable release inside or outside the peer range
A jQuery support-policy or OpenJS status change

projects.name: jQuery Migrate
projects.maintenanceStatement: The official upgrade guide presents Migrate as a temporary development aid whose uncompressed build reports compatibility warnings during staged upgrades.
projects.jqstarRole: Application owners may use the matching Migrate release while upgrading jQuery, preserve its warnings, fix each finding, and remove it when the stage is complete.
nonGoals: Treating warnings as universally safe automatic rewrites

projects.name: jQuery UI
projects.maintenanceStatement: jQuery UI receives compatibility, security, and important-regression maintenance, with no significant new feature work planned; OpenJS still classifies the project as Archived.
projects.jqstarRole: Existing applications may keep isolated jQuery UI regions during measured migration; new work uses jQStar's native semantic components.
nonGoals: A runtime dependency or source fork
Widget Factory, Widget Plugin Bridge, or third-party extension compatibility
ThemeRoller, effects, or imperative plugin API compatibility
recheckTriggers: A jQuery UI stable release or maintenance statement change

projects.name: jQuery Mobile
projects.maintenanceStatement: The official archived repository is read-only, states that jQuery Mobile is no longer maintained, and documents its old 1.4.x jQuery compatibility range.
projects.jqstarRole: Preserve semantic HTML, direct URLs, native links and forms, responsive layout, touch and keyboard access, progressive enhancement, and graceful degradation while migrating route by route without the Mobile runtime.
nonGoals: Loading, wrapping, forking, or emulating the archived runtime
Recreating its router, page model, virtual mouse, themes, widgets, or transition catalog
Running jQuery Mobile beside jQuery 4 in a modern document
recheckTriggers: A change to the official archived repository statement

projects.name: Sizzle
projects.maintenanceStatement: OpenJS classifies standalone Sizzle as Archived; selector behavior for jQStar comes from the application-owned jQuery peer regardless of jQuery's internal selector implementation.
projects.jqstarRole: No separate role. Real jQuery owns selector semantics.
nonGoals: A standalone dependency, fork, or selector-engine swap
Treating transitive TypeScript declarations as runtime integration

projects.name: QUnit
projects.maintenanceStatement: QUnit remains an active OpenJS At-Large project with current Node and browser releases.
projects.jqstarRole: An exact installed QUnit consumer runs jquery-star/testing conformance without changing the repository's Vitest, property, static, or Playwright quality stack.
nonGoals: Replacing the repository quality stack with QUnit
recheckTriggers: A QUnit stable release or support-policy change

uiCapabilityMap.contractDifference: Semantic headings and disclosure buttons replace Widget Factory methods, options, events, data instances, and theme classes.
The jQStar combobox uses native input and listbox semantics, source-owned markup, named actions, and a different data/request contract.
jQStar keeps native button semantics and does not expose the jQuery UI button plugin or theme classes.
Native buttons or pressed controls replace the retired imperative buttonset contract.
Native checkbox and radio inputs remain the submitted and accessible controls; no themeable-button plugin contract is reproduced.
Source-owned composition replaces automatic child-widget discovery, refresh, and corner-class management.
A labelled native input remains the form value while calendar and popover behavior use jQStar's documented component contracts.
The native dialog element and jQStar focus lifecycle replace the imperative dialog instance, option, event, overlay, and theme contracts.
Explicit menu-button or context-menu markup replaces automatic plugin initialization and jQuery UI event payloads.
Native progress semantics and documented state replace the themeable progressbar plugin.
The application chooses a native select or explicit listbox composition; no selectmenu method or theme contract is preserved.
A native range input remains authoritative and jQStar does not emulate the jQuery UI slider instance or events.
A native number input with explicit step controls replaces the spinner plugin API.
ARIA tabs and source-owned panels replace Widget Factory options, remote-loading behavior, and callback events.
The jQStar tooltip owns documented hover and focus semantics but does not preserve the jQuery UI tooltip API or theme.
jQStar has no generic arbitrary-element draggable API; specific components may own bounded pointer and keyboard behavior.
jQStar has no generic drop-target manager or draggable/droppable coordination contract.
jQStar component controllers use native pointer and keyboard events and do not publish the jQuery UI mouse abstraction.
The recipe exposes a bounded panel layout with named actions; it is not an arbitrary-element resizable plugin.
Semantic list, table, and form selections use their own native controls; no generic lasso selection API ships.
The source-owned sortable recipe includes keyboard movement and named actions and does not emulate connectWith, helper, or plugin event payloads.
Native reset behavior and component-owned listeners replace Widget Factory refresh callbacks.
jQStar components share internal floating placement but publish no general jQuery UI Position-compatible API.

uiCapabilityMap.legacyCapability: Effects, easings, class animation, and color animation
uiCapabilityMap.contractDifference: jQStar does not ship the jQuery UI effects catalog or its overloaded jQuery animation methods; application CSS must honor reduced motion.

uiCapabilityMap.legacyCapability: ThemeRoller and jQuery UI CSS class contract
uiCapabilityMap.contractDifference: jQStar uses its own CSS variables and source-owned component markup and does not consume or generate ThemeRoller classes.

uiCapabilityMap.legacyCapability: Widget Factory lifecycle, inheritance, options, methods, events, and data instances
uiCapabilityMap.contractDifference: jQStar's application, plugin, directive, action, and UI contracts are separate APIs and do not implement $.widget or Widget Factory inheritance.

uiCapabilityMap.legacyCapability: Widget Plugin Bridge and imperative jQuery plugin dispatch
uiCapabilityMap.contractDifference: Migration replaces string method dispatch, option bags, callback payloads, and jQuery data instances with semantic markup and documented jQStar APIs.

uiCapabilityMap.legacyCapability: Third-party Widget Factory extensions and application plugins
uiCapabilityMap.contractDifference: Legacy extensions remain application-owned during migration; compatibility is application-specific and never inferred from the official catalog.

requirements: Run exact installed QUnit conformance through jquery-star/testing
Keep QUnit out of runtime and testing bundle graphs
Keep Vitest, property, static, and Playwright gates authoritative
Detect only bounded declared metadata or schema-validated user summaries
Never inject Migrate, suppress warnings, or rewrite application code
Link to the official staged upgrade workflow
Build exact-package coexistence and representative migration evidence
Complete the catalog and API gap map without presuming an adapter
Keep jQuery UI absent from jQStar runtime, bundles, and source
Preserve progressive-enhancement needs in a modern route-level migration
Keep the archived runtime, router, page model, virtual mouse, themes, and widgets absent
Separate the jQuery Core upgrade from UI and navigation migration
